title: [IMP2-1] A stamped but unpublished Commit blocks every later Commit in the channel
description: Review finding IMP2-1: A stamped but unpublished Commit blocks every later Commit in the channel (lens IMP2). Location: spec/05-messaging.md:27, :30; spec/14-jmap.md:218, :222. Fix: The losing test at 05:27 is "an earlier position holds an `op` that opens under the same epoch's sealing key ... to a Commit". It needs only the sealing layer and the clear `content_type` (05:280), not a valid Commit, and it does not need the winner to be published. The sealing key is a per-epoch MLS exporter output (09:79), so any epoch-N member can trigger this, including a member about to be Removed. The republish clause at 14:222 ("any member holding the pair MAY publish it") covers only operation streams, because 14:218 sends commit stamps in the routing envelope instead. Fix: (1) the earliest stamped Commit that fully validates (unseal, MLS-decrypt, RFC 9420 validation) wins, and receivers skip invalid ones; (2) extend 14:222 to commit streams: any member that sees a valid stamped Commit in the log but not on the channel within T publishes it in a routing envelope it signs with the admission key, carrying the existing `commitStamp`. Full text: notes/review2/IMP2-verified.md and notes/review2/IMP2.md.
